The Clock of Ontology.pdf: Existence moves — but only if you know its hidden geometry. The Clock of Ontology does not study what exists — it maps how existence moves. Being, Meaning, civilizations, and individuals all follow a hidden geometry of motion: they rise, decay, and sometimes, escape. Modern life is not false. It is collapsed — detached from virtue, meaning, and alignment. Institutions thrive while producing decay, not through corruption, but through a reduced structure. This book reveals the ontic regions of order, blindness, decay, and resurrection. Mythologies are not mere stories — they are early maps of the same geometry, pointing the way to a third dimension of being: Flight, achievable only through precise alignment with Meaning (Logos). No preaching. No persuasion. No invented values. Only the structure of existence, waiting to be seen.
Democracy is Tyranny.pdf: This book advances a structural claim: democracy is not the negation of tyranny but its most advanced redesign. It does not abolish coercion; it reorganizes and conceals it. What was once a visible apex becomes an institutional backend, while power speaks in the language of participation and consent. The result is not moral critique but structural autopsy. Democracy is coercion after it has learned to disappear.
Law is Injustice.pdf: This book performs that question on law itself. It does not seek reform. It does not seek improvement. It does not accuse law of hypocrisy. It follows law to its structural end. Once the fiction of unconditioned agency is removed once determinism is taken seriously, juridical authority loses its anchor. Law continues to operate — but as what it is: a virtual machine sustained by fear, repetition, and the high cost of withdrawal. The claim is not emotional. It is architectural. Law does not fail to deliver justice. It delivers what it is built to produce: closure, enforcement, and the manufacture of guilt within a world that contains only causality. Remove the spell, and the title stops sounding extreme. Law is injustice.
Economics Kills the Value.pdf: Economics does not mismeasure value. It cannot perceive it. By replacing contribution with monetized activity, the discipline rewards circulation and blinds itself to what sustains life. Growth continues. Value disappears
Academia is Idolatry.pdf: The university does not primarily produce knowledge. It produces authorization. Recognition replaces reality constraint; procedure replaces truth. What passes is what belongs
Grim Reaper Burns Philosophy.pdf: Philosophy did not weaken. It was amputated. Logos was translated, classified, and replaced by procedure. What remains is a preserved corpse regulating what may count as real. This book performs the autopsy and sets the body on fire.
The Dark Book.pdf: The Matrix is not a regime but a structure of substitution that absorbs critique, upgrades through crisis, and survives by replacing reality with operational replicas. Reform feeds it. Revolution refreshes it. Drift erodes the human sensor for meaning until imitation becomes self-sustaining and virtue becomes intolerable. This book maps the machine to its terminal logic—autoimmunity, expansion without purpose, and a civilization defending itself against life.
The Treason of Philology.pdf: This book argues that modern philology did not fail to recover origins—it replaced the recovery of memory with the theater of method. Treating myths, names, and linguistic fragments as analyzable debris rather than as structural “black boxes” of civilizational memory, the discipline dissolved sequence into classification and mission into procedure. What claims to reconstruct the past instead prevents its reappearance. This is not an accusation of error but of structural betrayal: a science of origins that became autoimmune against origin itself.
How Morality Replaced Reality.pdf: Morality is not tested as good or bad, but as real or dependent. This book treats moral systems as participation-based structures—sustained by recognition, enforcement, and identity roles—and shows how modernity elevated them into ontology. When rules present themselves as reality, dissent becomes heresy and exit becomes impossible. This is not a critique of morality, but a diagnosis of its transformation into a machine indistinguishable from being.
Humanity is the Enemy.pdf: The threat is not outside the system—it is the system’s human core. This book argues that what is called “humanity” has become a self-reinforcing structure that replaces reality.

This is not a book about miracles. It is a reconstruction. *The Handbook of Magic* reclaims “magic” from superstition and spectacle, restoring it to its original meaning: the hidden architecture of reality itself. Moving through ancient names, broken symbols, and forgotten axes of meaning, this work challenges the foundations of religion, language, and history—revealing a world that was not erased, but amputated. Enter not as a reader, but as a participant. This is not information. This is structure.
